summary: Slab/buddy allocator public memory allocation. Round-robins through the linked list of allocator contexts starting at off_5E9988, scanning each context's 8-byte free descriptors and carving a block with sub_594E1A; the descriptor start is shrunk and the cursor global updated on success. When no existing context fits, falls back to the static pool list headed by off_5E7968, and if a pool has spare descriptors commits pages with VirtualAlloc, zeroes them via sub_58BB10, and splits them into chained 4KB blocks recorded in the pool's descriptor table; if every pool is exhausted it creates a new allocator via SlabBuddyAllocatorInitialization and returns its first 256-byte block. Returns the allocated pointer (page base + 256) or 0 on failure.

local_names.v1: cursor into the linked list of allocator contexts
local_names.v2: context page-base word; -1 marks an exhausted context
local_names.v3: context descriptor cursor / page-base derivation input
local_names.v4: 4KB page address derived from the descriptor's offset
local_names.v5: carried request size used in carve and shrink operations
local_names.v7: cursor into the static pool list headed by off_5E7968
local_names.i: first page of the region being committed/carved

operations.description: v1 = off_5E9988 seeds the round-robin cursor from the allocator-context list
Walk the singly linked list of allocator contexts (v1 = *(char**)v1) until the cursor returns to off_5E9988
A context whose page-base word v2 == -1 marks an exhausted context; the request size v5 is carried unchanged into the pool fallback
v3 = *(v1 + 2) loads the context's descriptor cursor; v4 = v2 + 4096 * ((v3 - v1 - 24) >> 3) derives the 4KB page address from the descriptor's offset within the context's descriptor table
Scan 8-byte free descriptors (start/size pairs) from v3 while v3 < v1 + 8216; a usable block needs *(v3) >= a1 and *(v3 + 1) > a1 so its span covers the request

sub_594E1A(v4, *(v3), a1) carves a block of size a1 from the page; on success the cursor global off_5E9988 is updated to v1, the descriptor start *(v3) is shrunk by v5, the new cursor *(v1 + 2) = v3 is stored, and the carved pointer is returned
When sub_594E1A fails, the descriptor's high bound *(v3 + 1) is lowered to a1 and the scan advances (v3 += 8, page v4 += 4096)
A second scan from the descriptor-table base (v1 + 24) up to the recorded cursor v17 re-tries the tail of the table with the same carve-or-shrink logic
When no existing context fits, walk the static pool list headed by off_5E7968 looking for a pool whose page base is valid and whose descriptor table is non-empty (*(v7 + 3) non-zero)

When the pool list is exhausted, SlabBuddyAllocatorInitialization() creates a new allocator context; on success its first 256-byte block is set up (header size 240, next-free pointer, pool free-space decrement) and v16 + 256 is returned
Return 0 when neither an existing context nor a fresh allocator can satisfy the request
v8 = *(v7 + 3) reads the pool's free-descriptor cursor; locate the first descriptor whose word is -1 (v20 counts the page index)
VirtualAlloc(i, v20 << 12, 0x1000, 4) commits the selected pages; a return different from i fails the allocation (return 0)
sub_58BB10(i, 0, 0) zero-initializes the freshly committed pages
Split the committed region into 4KB blocks chained through size headers/footers (payload 240, footer -1 sentinel, next-block pointers) and record each block pair in the pool's descriptor table
off_5E9988 is updated to the current pool, the pool's free-descriptor cursor *(v7 + 3) is advanced, the request size a1 is stored in the page header byte, and *(v7 + 2) records the descriptor start
*v8 -= a1 and i[1] -= a1 shrink the pool's free-space bookkeeping; the returned pointer result = i + 64 lies 256 bytes into the first page
Return the allocated pointer (i + 64) or 0 when page commit or allocator creation failed
Invoked by the frame-path allocator users sub_58A973, sub_58AB58 and sub_58B5D4

if (v7 == &off_5E7968) { v15 = SlabBuddyAllocatorInitialization(); if (v15) { setup header; return v16 + 256; } return 0; }
